subject: Clarifying how prefetch/prefix hits are metered and contract addendum
messages:
From: Evelyn Ross <evelyn.ross@cloudledger.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: how will you meter / bill prefix/prefetch cache hits?

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudLedger is excited about Redwood's throughput and the prefix caching demo looked promising for our high-repeat workflows. Before we move to a procurement review I need one thing clarified for our finance and legal teams: how does Redwood meter and bill requests that are satisfied entirely from the prefix/prefetch cache?

Two concrete examples that came up in our internal review:
1) A user request where the application prepends a fixed 150-token system prompt + a 20-token user prompt and the cached response matches exactly (no model compute). Do you bill input tokens, output tokens, neither, or some per-request fee?
2) A partial hit where the first 100 tokens of the prompt are served from cache but the remainder requires model inference. How is that invoiced?

We are optimizing for predictable per-seat economics and need to know whether heavy reuse (high cache hit rates) reduces our billed token volume. Appreciate a short note or a pointer to the official billing wording we can include in the SOW.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Ross
Head of ML Platform | CloudLedger

Subject: Fwd: CloudLedger billing question — pricing guidance?

Jasmine / Marissa,

Evelyn's questions are straightforward but finance/legal will want hard wording. Two commercial points for us to decide:
- Do we treat full cache hits as non-billable token volume (i.e., no input/output token charge) or do we bill a small per-request "lookup" unit?
- If we do the latter, what unit price keeps incentives aligned (we should still make cache hits materially cheaper than inference so customers prefer caching)?

My instinct: for enterprise named accounts we give full cache-hit token forgiveness (no token charge) and instead count them against a request cap in the contract. For hosted plans we can keep a small per-lookup charge (e.g., 0.0005 USD) to discourage abuse.

Thoughts? If you agree I can draft SOW language + a short table of examples.

—Karthik
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudLedger billing question — pricing guidance?

Agree with Karthik on the commercial approach. For CloudLedger (enterprise, committed) propose:
- Full-prefix cache hits: no per-token charge. They count against a separate "lookup" metric that is tracked but only used for overage billing if they exceed committed QPS/request cap.
- Partial hits: bill tokens for the non-cached portion (both input tokens that required model attention + generated output tokens).
- Edge case: if a request results in an identical cached response but the customer requests a freshness re-eval or instructs the model to regenerate, standard inference billing applies.

I'll prepare sample SOW language and a brief addendum for legal. Also recommend we offer a 3-month usage credit against lookup overages during onboarding (helps procurement).

Marissa Cole
Senior Deals Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Legal Team <legal@cloudledger.com>

Subject: Re: Question: how will you meter / bill prefix/prefetch cache hits?

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the clear examples. Below is the billing policy we propose to include in the SOW and your procurement bundle. I'll call out the two example scenarios you sent with numbers to make it concrete.

Redwood proposed metering policy (draft language):
1) Full-prefix cache hit: If a request is satisfied entirely from the prefix/prefetch cache and the response is returned without invoking model inference, Redwood does not charge per-token fees for input or output tokens for that request. The request is recorded against the customer's cache-lookup metric. Cache-lookup units are visible in the Redwood Console and counted toward any committed lookup cap.

2) Partial cache hit: If a request is partially satisfied from cache and the model is invoked to compute the remainder, Redwood charges for the model-invoked portion only. Billed units include the tokens processed by the model for the non-cached portion (input tokens that required inference and any generated output tokens).

3) Regeneration/freshness override: If the client explicitly requests regeneration (e.g., via force_refresh flag) or otherwise triggers a execution path that bypasses the cache for freshness, normal inference billing applies.

4) Hosted vs. enterprise: For hosted self-serve customers, cache lookup requests are counted and billed at a nominal per-lookup fee after free tiers to prevent abuse. For named enterprise commitments (e.g., CloudLedger's reserved capacity deal) Redwood will waive per-lookup charges and include lookup tracking only for observability and overage enforcement.

Examples (illustrative numbers):
- Example A (full hit): 150-token static system prompt + 20-token user prompt -> cache returns 200-token response with no model compute. Billing: 0 tokens billed; 1 cache-lookup recorded.
- Example B (partial hit): first 100 tokens from cache, remaining 70 tokens require model inference which generates 150 tokens. Billing: tokens billed = 70 (input consumed by model) + 150 (generated output) = 220 tokens billed.

Attached: redwood_ratecard_Q3_v2.xlsx (shows nominal per-lookup fee for hosted plans and lookup tracking columns), prefix_cache_spec.pdf (technical flow).

If this looks good to you I can have this language inserted into the SOW as an addendum. Marissa — looping you and legal for insertion guidance and the onboarding credit language (we propose 3 months free for lookup overages).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
